classificationTaxonomy.meaning: A reusable entity, callable boundary, or typed result with an independently identifiable responsibility and supported contract boundary.
classificationTaxonomy.filesystemEffect: A distinct logical module or contract surface; it may still participate in an owning Aggregate.
classificationTaxonomy.applicability: Framework baseline; consumers specialize or implement it as required.

classificationTaxonomy.meaning: A required responsibility whose semantic ownership belongs to a specific Entity/Aggregate and whose completeness depends on that owner.
classificationTaxonomy.filesystemEffect: Allocated inside the owning Aggregate boundary; internal files/submodules may be separated without transferring ownership.
classificationTaxonomy.applicability: Required for every instance of the owning Aggregate.

classificationTaxonomy.meaning: A reusable specialized capability or contract selected only when a concrete consumer/Step needs that pattern.
classificationTaxonomy.filesystemEffect: An optional cohesive submodule/package; no mandatory dependency for consumers that do not select it.
classificationTaxonomy.applicability: Mandatory only after the concrete specialization selects the pattern and its applicable contracts.

classificationTaxonomy.meaning: Cross-cutting architectural invariants, conformance obligations, or review material that does not define a standalone runtime component.
classificationTaxonomy.filesystemEffect: Documentation/conformance material; do not create runtime managers, services, interfaces or state machines merely to represent the guidance.
classificationTaxonomy.applicability: Applicable rules may be binding when the corresponding pattern or lifecycle behavior is selected.

classificationTaxonomy.meaning: A contract or model whose domain, workflow, artifact semantics or explicit scope belongs to one reference consumer.
classificationTaxonomy.filesystemEffect: Excluded from GPWCF Core and its generic Public API; retained with the consumer.

governingAllocationDecisions: Stage and Step are separate architectural Entities/Aggregates with distinct callable boundaries and ownership.
Stage Composition is a mandatory responsibility owned by Stage; it coordinates Steps only through their public Step contracts.
Step Composition is a mandatory responsibility owned by Step; it coordinates SPUs and selected Supporting Units internally.
SPU is a mandatory standalone processing boundary with its own specialized input/output and SPUExecutionResult.
SPUExecutionResult and StepExecutionResult are distinct standalone typed result contracts with different producers, consumers and scopes.
Stage Flow Result is an independent Stage-owned result contract, but its concrete structure is Stage-specific; no universal FlowResult schema is established.
Validator, Observation and Error Handling are optional reusable patterns. Their behavioral, association, lifecycle and result contracts remain specialized.

No universal SupportingUnit base type, common behavioral contract, plugin manager, loader, association manager, lifecycle manager, registry, scheduler or generic result model is justified by this inventory.
The two Common Step Composition coordination contracts are conformance guidance, not runtime components. Their applicable obligations can be mandatory without creating common runtime infrastructure.
The Common Error Model is Generator-scoped despite its Common folder location and is excluded from generic Core.
The Step Error Model is semantic rather than executable; its current generic reuse is conditional because it directly depends on the Generator-scoped Common Error Model.

The Stage and SPU architecture documents contain generic responsibilities alongside error-model clauses tied to the consumer-scoped Common Error Model; their generic sections and error-specific sections must be separated in subsequent boundary work.
Prefect is the accepted initial integration target. Prefect-specific execution realization belongs only in the Prefect Integration boundary; its adoption is not under reconsideration.

artifactAllocations.title: Pipeline Stage-Level Architecture
artifactAllocations.runtimeNature: Defines Stage facade, Stage Composition ownership, Step coordination, Stage flow semantics and Stage-owned Flow Result; it does not mandate a separate facade or composition class.
artifactAllocations.genericity: partially_generic; StageError and StageErrorTypeDefinitionRegistry clauses depend on the currently Generator-scoped Common Error Model
artifactAllocations.allocationDisposition: Allocate generic Stage aggregate semantics to Core; isolate or generalize StageError/registry-specific clauses before treating the entire document as a generic Core dependency.
artifactAllocations.prefectAlignment: Stage semantic ownership and Step-facing boundaries remain Core; native Stage Parent Workflow execution and runtime mapping belong to integrations.prefect.
artifactAllocations.allocationRationale: Stage is a generic aggregate that owns Step membership, coordination and flow-result semantics. Its error-model integration is not generic merely because it appears in the Stage architecture.

artifactAllocations.title: Pipeline Stage Step-Level Architecture
artifactAllocations.architecturalOwner: Step Aggregate and its internal processing boundary
artifactAllocations.runtimeNature: Structural architecture for Step, Step Composition, SPUs, optional supporting patterns and distinct result boundaries; not itself a runtime component.
artifactAllocations.genericity: mostly_generic; individual error-model clauses inherit the conditional genericity of their referenced error contracts
artifactAllocations.allocationDisposition: Use as the structural source for multiple modules; do not allocate it as one executable component or treat every listed supporting pattern as mandatory.
artifactAllocations.prefectAlignment: Preserve Stage -> Step public invocation and Step-owned internal composition; Prefect realizes native nested execution but does not own GPWCF semantics.
artifactAllocations.allocationRationale: This document describes the Step aggregate and its specialized collaborators; its content must be decomposed by actual ownership rather than copied into a single package.

artifactAllocations.title: Step Contract
artifactAllocations.runtimeNature: Stable Stage-facing callable boundary; execute(input: TInput) -> StepExecutionResult[TOutput].
artifactAllocations.allocationDisposition: Core standalone entity contract; its public supported form is exposed through Core Public API, while concrete Step implementations remain consumer specializations.
artifactAllocations.prefectAlignment: Integration binds the Step public callable boundary to a native Step Subworkflow; native execution does not replace the Step contract.
artifactAllocations.allocationRationale: Step has an independently consumable Stage-facing boundary and owns its internal composition; it must not be buried as an implementation detail of Stage.

artifactAllocations.title: Step Composition Contract
artifactAllocations.runtimeNature: Mandatory internal composition responsibility for SPU/supporting-unit selection, invocation coordination, Step-specific flow decisions, evidence retention and result assembly; a separate public runtime class is not mandated.
artifactAllocations.allocationDisposition: Place within the Step-owned module boundary; internal submodules may be split by cohesion, but ownership remains with Step.
artifactAllocations.prefectAlignment: Prefect may execute the native Step Subworkflow and its child tasks; Step Composition retains semantic authority and does not become a second scheduler.
artifactAllocations.allocationRationale: Composition is an obligatory responsibility owned by the Step Aggregate, not a peer standalone component or universal composition framework.

artifactAllocations.title: Step Processing Unit Contract
artifactAllocations.runtimeNature: Actual specialized processing boundary; execute(input: TInput) -> SPUExecutionResult[TOutput].
artifactAllocations.genericity: partially_generic; generic callable/result semantics are Core candidates, while error type definitions, SPUError production and Pipeline-owned Registry clauses depend on Common/Error_Model.json
artifactAllocations.allocationDisposition: Allocate the generic SPU callable contract to Core. Treat errorOwnershipAndProduction and dependent errorHandlingResultProduction as a conditional extension until the error model is generalized or decoupled.
artifactAllocations.prefectAlignment: Bind the SPU's executable responsibility to a native task within its owning Step execution; Prefect Task Run identity/state remains operational evidence.
artifactAllocations.allocationRationale: SPU is a real independently specialized processing unit, not a delegation-only wrapper. Its current error-specific clauses must not silently make the entire Core contract depend on Generator-specific registries.

artifactAllocations.title: SPUExecutionResult Contract
artifactAllocations.runtimeNature: Independent typed result for one normally completed SPU invocation; produced by the concrete SPU and consumed by Step Composition.
artifactAllocations.allocationDisposition: Core result type; retain its per-SPU invocation scope and do not merge it with StepExecutionResult.
artifactAllocations.prefectAlignment: Integration transports/maps the typed domain result across native task execution; Prefect Task state does not replace it.
artifactAllocations.allocationRationale: The result has an independent semantic boundary and producer, and is not an internal field of the Step aggregate result.

artifactAllocations.title: StepExecutionResult Contract
artifactAllocations.runtimeNature: Independent Stage-facing result for one Step invocation; assembled by the concrete Step/Step Composition.
artifactAllocations.genericity: generic_core_contract_with_optional_pattern_specific_result_slots; errorResult currently depends on the conditional Step Error Model and its Generator-scoped error-model dependency
artifactAllocations.allocationDisposition: Core result boundary is mandatory and standalone. Keep each optional result slot independently optional and preserve specialized result contracts; resolve whether slots remain direct fields or are specialized generically during Public API design.
artifactAllocations.prefectAlignment: Integration retrieves/maps this domain result from native Step execution; Prefect operational State is never a substitute.
artifactAllocations.allocationRationale: The Step result is an independent contract with a different scope from SPUExecutionResult. Optional result fields do not make the supporting patterns mandatory.

artifactAllocations.title: Step Error Model Contract
artifactAllocations.architecturalOwner: Step-specific Error Model semantics; physical ErrorResult assembly remains with Step Composition
artifactAllocations.runtimeNature: Semantic contract defining ErrorResult structure and occurrence aggregation; explicitly not an executable node or separate aggregation runtime object.
artifactAllocations.genericity: conditionally_reusable; directly references SPUError, SPUErrorTypeDefinitionReference and Registry concepts from the currently Generator-scoped Common Error Model
artifactAllocations.allocationDisposition: Do not admit its current dependency closure into generic Core as-is. Retain as an optional pattern contract and generalize/detach the referenced error model before Core allocation.
artifactAllocations.prefectAlignment: Remains a domain result/semantic contract; it is not bound to a Prefect task or node.
artifactAllocations.allocationRationale: A Step may choose this model; it does not apply to every Step. Its semantic generality is constrained by a direct dependency on a consumer-scoped error vocabulary and registry.

artifactAllocations.title: Step Supporting Error Handling Unit Behavioral Contract
artifactAllocations.architecturalOwner: Selected Error Handling Unit pattern under Step Composition
artifactAllocations.runtimeNature: Optional executable supporting-unit behavior with its own invocation, operation-result, provenance and custody semantics; not a universal SupportingUnit base type.
artifactAllocations.allocationDisposition: Optional reusable pattern; include only when selected by a concrete Step.
artifactAllocations.prefectAlignment: When selected, bind its executable operation to a native executable element under the owning Step; keep its specialized result/custody semantics in Core.
artifactAllocations.allocationRationale: Behavior and result semantics are specialized and differ from Validator and Observation; no common behavioral abstraction is justified.

artifactAllocations.title: Error Handling Unit Operation Execution Contract
artifactAllocations.architecturalOwner: Concrete Error Handling Unit; Step Composition owns association/lifecycle coordination
artifactAllocations.runtimeNature: Detailed callable/input/operation-result/attempt identity/target access/publication protocol for a selected Error Handling Unit.
artifactAllocations.genericity: pattern_specific_reusable; publication/occurrence references are coupled to the optional Step Error Model and its current error vocabulary
artifactAllocations.allocationDisposition: Optional pattern module; preserve specialized operation and publication semantics. Keep Common Error Model dependency conditional rather than imposing it on Core consumers that do not select this pattern.
artifactAllocations.prefectAlignment: Bind actual handling operations only when selected; Prefect supplies execution mechanics, not operation-result meaning or custody rules.
artifactAllocations.allocationRationale: This is a specialized executable behavior contract, not a general-purpose error manager or global pipeline service.

artifactAllocations.title: Step Supporting Error Handling Unit Association Contract
artifactAllocations.runtimeNature: Specialized relationship contract governing applicability to Step-defined targets, identity, multiplicity, invocation binding, change, dissociation and history; not an Association Manager.
artifactAllocations.allocationDisposition: Include only for Error Handling specializations that use the defined target association model.
artifactAllocations.prefectAlignment: Use native relationship/invocation constructs only where semantically appropriate; the contract's Association meaning remains GPWCF-owned.
artifactAllocations.allocationRationale: Association is a specialized mechanism for this pattern, not the general functional-binding objective.

artifactAllocations.title: Step Supporting Error Handling Unit Lifecycle Contract
artifactAllocations.architecturalOwner: Concrete Step Composition for decisions; Error Handling Unit for its technical lifecycle mechanics
artifactAllocations.runtimeNature: Pattern-specific readiness/admission/operation/publication custody/quiescence/reuse/release obligations; no generic LifecycleManager.
artifactAllocations.allocationDisposition: Applicable only when an Error Handling Unit instance is selected and lifecycle-managed under this specialization.
artifactAllocations.prefectAlignment: Prefect run/task lifecycle is operational and cannot replace Unit-specific lifecycle, custody or release semantics.
artifactAllocations.allocationRationale: The specialized contract adds operation and Publisher/Reservation lifetimes that cannot be generalized into a common lifecycle implementation.

artifactAllocations.title: ErrorHandlerResult Contract
artifactAllocations.runtimeNature: Distinct result aggregating accepted error-handling operation entries and targeted occurrence references; it is not ErrorResult.
artifactAllocations.genericity: pattern_specific_reusable; occurrence references depend on the Step Error Model's occurrence identity vocabulary
artifactAllocations.allocationDisposition: Optional pattern result; preserve independent identity and custody semantics and do not merge with ErrorResult.
artifactAllocations.prefectAlignment: Map as a domain result across native execution; Prefect State does not replace it.
artifactAllocations.allocationRationale: It represents handling activity results, not the original error occurrences; it belongs with the optional Error Handling pattern.

artifactAllocations.title: OperationEntryPublisher Contract
artifactAllocations.runtimeNature: Composition-owned publication capability defining reservation-backed atomic acceptance, status resolution, release, failure, concurrency, ordering and invocation closure; not a global publisher service.
artifactAllocations.allocationDisposition: Optional Error Handling sub-capability; mandatory only for concrete Steps selecting this publication protocol.
artifactAllocations.prefectAlignment: Prefect may execute the Unit and transport returned state, but does not replace atomic publication acceptance, ownership transfer or recovery semantics.
artifactAllocations.allocationRationale: The Publisher is owned by the Step-specific Error Handling Composition and is not an independent global framework manager.

artifactAllocations.title: PublicationReservation Contract
artifactAllocations.runtimeNature: Opaque single-use publication capability binding one reservation to exactly one operation entry; not a general reservation manager.
artifactAllocations.allocationDisposition: Allocate with the optional Error Handling publication protocol; never expose as a general GPWCF resource reservation abstraction.
artifactAllocations.prefectAlignment: Native Prefect execution cannot be treated as proof that a reservation was consumed or ownership was transferred.
artifactAllocations.allocationRationale: Its semantics are inseparable from the specialized Publisher protocol and complete-entry custody transfer.

artifactAllocations.title: Single Step Publication and Result-Retention Specialization Contract
artifactAllocations.architecturalOwner: Concrete Single Step specialization; Step-specific Recovery Owner and publication implementation
artifactAllocations.runtimeNature: Reusable specialization obligations, instantiated by a concrete Single Step only when it selects ErrorHandlingUnit plus OperationEntryPublisher publication.
artifactAllocations.genericity: reusable_specialization_rule; concrete protocol types, recovery procedure, identity and retention policies are consumer-Step-specific
artifactAllocations.allocationDisposition: Keep the generic specialization requirements as a pattern contract; concrete instances and their operational choices remain with the consumer's Step specialization.
artifactAllocations.prefectAlignment: Prefect does not own recovery custody or publication identity; integration must preserve the Step-defined protocol across native execution.
artifactAllocations.allocationRationale: The specialization contract is reusable, but the actual specialization values and Recovery Owner belong to the concrete Single Step. It is not mandatory for Steps that do not use this path.

artifactAllocations.title: Step Supporting Validator Unit Behavioral Contract
artifactAllocations.architecturalOwner: Selected Validator Unit pattern under Step Composition
artifactAllocations.runtimeNature: Optional executable validation behavior with its own invocation, validation result and provenance semantics.
artifactAllocations.allocationDisposition: Optional reusable pattern; not required for every Step or SPU.
artifactAllocations.prefectAlignment: When selected, bind validation execution to a native executable element while preserving validation result semantics and owning Step coordination.
artifactAllocations.allocationRationale: Validation behavior is distinct from processing and observation; its specialized result must not be unified with other Supporting Unit outputs.

artifactAllocations.title: Step Supporting Validator Unit Association Contract
artifactAllocations.runtimeNature: Specialized relationship contract between a Validator Unit instance and Step-defined processing target scope(s).
artifactAllocations.allocationDisposition: Applicable only when the selected Validator specialization uses target associations.
artifactAllocations.prefectAlignment: Association is realized through a semantically suitable native relationship or invocation binding; it is not a mandatory Prefect construct.
artifactAllocations.allocationRationale: The association is Validator-specific and remains owned/coordinated by Step Composition.

artifactAllocations.title: Step Supporting Validator Unit Lifecycle Contract
artifactAllocations.architecturalOwner: Concrete Step Composition for lifecycle decisions; Validator Unit for technical mechanics
artifactAllocations.runtimeNature: Validator-specific readiness, invocation, quiescence, reuse, release and evidence custody obligations.
artifactAllocations.allocationDisposition: Applicable only when the Validator Unit pattern is selected and lifecycle obligations apply.
artifactAllocations.prefectAlignment: Native task completion is not equivalent to Validator instance release or evidence custody settlement.
artifactAllocations.allocationRationale: The Validator has its own technical lifecycle semantics; common guidance supplies invariants, not a shared lifecycle manager.

artifactAllocations.title: Step Supporting Observation Unit Behavioral Contract
artifactAllocations.architecturalOwner: Selected Observation Unit pattern under Step Composition
artifactAllocations.runtimeNature: Optional observation activity with its own output/event, provenance and custody semantics; observation records are not part of StepExecutionResult by default.
artifactAllocations.allocationDisposition: Optional reusable pattern; keep observation outputs separate from processing and validation results.
artifactAllocations.prefectAlignment: Bind only the selected observation activity; preserve event/activity identity and result destination independently of Prefect task state.
artifactAllocations.allocationRationale: Observation may emit zero, one or many records and may use callbacks/subscriptions; it cannot share a generic result model with Validator or Error Handling.

artifactAllocations.title: Step Supporting Observation Unit Association Contract
artifactAllocations.runtimeNature: Specialized association to Step-owned observation target scopes with historical identity and provenance preservation.
artifactAllocations.allocationDisposition: Applicable only when the selected Observation Unit uses target associations.
artifactAllocations.prefectAlignment: Use native relationship mechanisms only when their semantics match; preserve capture-time context and association provenance.
artifactAllocations.allocationRationale: Observation association has its own target, activity and historical-provenance semantics.

artifactAllocations.title: Step Supporting Observation Unit Lifecycle Contract
artifactAllocations.architecturalOwner: Concrete Step Composition for lifecycle decisions; Observation Unit for technical activity mechanics
artifactAllocations.runtimeNature: Observation-specific readiness, activation, ongoing activity/subscription, quiescence, callback/queue reconciliation, reuse and release obligations.
artifactAllocations.allocationDisposition: Applicable only when the Observation Unit pattern is selected and lifecycle-managed.
artifactAllocations.prefectAlignment: Prefect Flow/Task termination does not by itself prove observation subscriptions, callbacks, queued records or evidence custody are settled.
artifactAllocations.allocationRationale: Long-lived observation activity and output retention require specialized lifecycle semantics rather than a universal lifecycle interface.

artifactAllocations.title: Step Composition Association Coordination Contract
artifactAllocations.architecturalOwner: Concrete Step Composition as conformance authority; framework documentation owns the shared invariants
artifactAllocations.runtimeNature: Documentation-level cross-cutting invariants for identity roles, target scope, multiplicity, invocation binding and dissociation; explicitly not an Association Manager, registry or runtime component.
artifactAllocations.allocationDisposition: Place in architectural guidance/conformance material. Applicable invariants are binding when a selected specialized contract uses associations, but no runtime module is created.
artifactAllocations.prefectAlignment: Relationship mechanisms are chosen by semantics; Functional Binding and Hierarchical Nesting do not require Association.
artifactAllocations.allocationRationale: It defines reusable conformance invariants and coordination ownership, not a standalone executable capability.

artifactAllocations.title: Step Composition Internal Component Lifecycle Coordination Contract
artifactAllocations.architecturalOwner: Concrete Step Composition as lifecycle decision authority
artifactAllocations.runtimeNature: Documentation-level lifecycle invariants for readiness, admission, identity/lifetimes, quiescence, reuse, release and evidence independence; explicitly rejects a universal lifecycle manager/interface/state machine.
artifactAllocations.allocationDisposition: Place in architectural guidance/conformance material. Its applicable rules may be mandatory for a selected component specialization, without creating a runtime lifecycle module.
artifactAllocations.prefectAlignment: Prefect operational state/lifecycle is not a substitute for GPWCF component lifecycle, custody or safe settlement.
artifactAllocations.allocationRationale: The obligations are cross-cutting conformance rules; specialized units retain their own technical lifecycle mechanics.

artifactAllocations.title: Pipeline Common Error Model
artifactAllocations.runtimeNature: Defines Stage/SPU error definitions, occurrences, registries and Pipeline ownership for Generator Pipeline participants.
artifactAllocations.genericity: explicitly_consumer_scoped; scope.appliesTo says every Stage and SPU participating in a Generator Pipeline
artifactAllocations.allocationDisposition: Exclude from generic GPWCF Core. Any future generalization requires a separate reviewed contract and explicit dependency-closure analysis; do not promote it based on the Common folder name.
artifactAllocations.prefectAlignment: Neither a Prefect runtime component nor a Prefect result/state model; domain error semantics remain consumer-owned unless generalized by an approved GPWCF contract.
artifactAllocations.allocationRationale: The declared scope is Generator Pipeline-specific. Its location under Common does not make it a framework-wide contract.

artifactAllocations.title: Supporting Pattern Integration Review
artifactAllocations.runtimeNature: Review record establishing that the three behavioral patterns remain specialized and that only association/lifecycle coordination invariants are shared.
artifactAllocations.allocationDisposition: Retain as design rationale/conformance guidance, not a runtime package or executable contract.
artifactAllocations.prefectAlignment: Supports binding selected executable supporting functions to native elements while preserving each specialized contract; no common plugin or SupportingUnit runtime.
artifactAllocations.allocationRationale: A review explains and justifies allocation decisions; it does not itself define an executable capability.

artifactAllocations.title: Step Termination and Lifecycle-Boundary Integration Review
artifactAllocations.runtimeNature: Review consolidating ownership of Stage disposition, Step public lifecycle boundary, Step Composition internal settlement and specialized unit obligations.
artifactAllocations.allocationDisposition: Use as conformance/review evidence; do not create a LifecycleManager or treat the review as a separate runtime module.
artifactAllocations.prefectAlignment: Prefect cancellation/termination is operational evidence; GPWCF Step settlement and release confirmation remain domain obligations.
artifactAllocations.allocationRationale: The review clarifies existing ownership and specialization obligations without adding a new runtime contract.

artifactAllocations.title: Pipeline Architecture and Stage Interface Contract
artifactAllocations.runtimeNature: Normative cross-stage contract for the Generator's thirteen-stage artifact pipeline, data ownership, identities, artifacts and stage dependencies.
artifactAllocations.allocationDisposition: Exclude from GPWCF Core, its public API and generic package tree. It remains a reference-consumer artifact.
artifactAllocations.prefectAlignment: Its Stage numbering, artifacts and execution dependencies must not be mapped mechanically to GPWCF Steps/SPUs or Prefect deployment topology.
artifactAllocations.allocationRationale: The contract explicitly defines the Generator's Stage 1–13 workflow and artifact domain; it is not a generic Pipeline/Root contract for GPWCF.

identifiedContractGaps.subject: Stage public callable contract
identifiedContractGaps.finding: Stage facade is defined as an architectural role and Stage owns its composition, but no separate Stage callable contract, concrete callable signature or production facade type is identified.
identifiedContractGaps.impact: Do not claim that a complete standalone Stage callable contract already exists. The Stage Core module boundary must expose the Stage role while a dedicated callable contract/specialization is defined in a later contract-design step.
identifiedContractGaps.disposition: Track for Stage Public API and module-boundary design; do not invent a signature in this classification document.

identifiedContractGaps.subject: Stage Flow Result specialization
identifiedContractGaps.finding: Flow Result is explicitly independent of StepExecutionResult and owned by Stage Composition, but its exact structure and composition policy are intentionally Stage-specific; no common schema is defined.
identifiedContractGaps.impact: Represent the responsibility as mandatory within each Stage Aggregate, but do not create a universal generic FlowResult type or schema.
identifiedContractGaps.disposition: Each concrete Stage specialization defines its own Flow Result contract and mapping.

identifiedContractGaps.subject: Generic GPWCF Pipeline Root callable contract
identifiedContractGaps.finding: No separate generic GPWCF Pipeline Root callable/composition contract is identified. The selected external workflow runtime owns native Root Flow and pipeline-level orchestration.
identifiedContractGaps.impact: Do not create a GPWCF Root Entity, Root Composition package or root-association runtime merely because Prefect has a Root Flow.
identifiedContractGaps.disposition: Keep Pipeline Root orchestration in the consumer/external workflow runtime unless a future generic GPWCF requirement establishes otherwise.

identifiedContractGaps.subject: Genericity of Stage/SPU/Step error semantics
identifiedContractGaps.finding: The Common Error Model explicitly applies to Generator Pipeline Stages/SPUs. Stage-Level Architecture and SPU Contract include error-definition/occurrence/Registry responsibilities that reference it; Step Error Model depends on SPUError and its Registry reference.
identifiedContractGaps.impact: A naive move of these entire documents into Core would import consumer-specific semantics and dependencies into the generic framework.
identifiedContractGaps.disposition: In Framework_Module_Boundary_Model, separate generic callable/composition semantics from error-model-specific clauses. Generalize or detach the error contracts only through an explicit later contract decision; do not modify specialized contracts in this phase.

identifiedContractGaps.subject: StepExecutionResult optional specialized result slots
identifiedContractGaps.finding: The mandatory StepExecutionResult contract includes independently optional processingArtifact, validatorResult, errorResult and errorHandlerResult fields. Their detailed schemas remain Step/pattern-specialized, and observation outputs are excluded by default.
identifiedContractGaps.impact: The Core result boundary is mandatory, but optional pattern result types must not force installation/import of every supporting pattern. ErrorResult additionally inherits the current Common Error Model genericity issue.
identifiedContractGaps.disposition: Resolve lazy/optional typing and extension boundaries in Dependency_and_Public_API_Architecture without changing the existing specialized result semantics here.

identifiedContractGaps.subject: Concrete Single Step publication specialization
identifiedContractGaps.finding: A concrete Single Step that selects ErrorHandlingUnits and OperationEntryPublisher must instantiate protocol result types, non-throwing ownership transfer, named Recovery Owner/procedure, identity rules and publication-status retention. A Step that does not select this path records non-applicability instead.
identifiedContractGaps.impact: The generic framework contract is reusable, but concrete specialization instances and recovery policy remain consumer Step responsibilities.
identifiedContractGaps.disposition: Do not create artificial Publisher infrastructure for Steps that do not select the publication path.

identifiedContractGaps.subject: Documented contracts versus executable GPWCF implementation
identifiedContractGaps.finding: The current baseline records no executable production Stage/Step/SPU runtime classes; the Python project entry point is empty and Core requirements declare standard-library-only dependencies.
identifiedContractGaps.impact: This matrix allocates documented responsibilities and contracts, not existing implementation files or verified production capabilities.
identifiedContractGaps.disposition: Filesystem implementation and structural/import verification occur only after the PHASE-03 design artifacts are reviewed and accepted.

prefectIntegrationAllocation.decision: Prefect 3.9.2 is the accepted initial pinned external workflow runtime under ADR-GPWCF-PREFECT-001; this classification does not reopen that decision.
coreResponsibilities: Stage and Step domain identities and callable semantics
Stage and Step composition ownership and transition meanings
SPU and selected Supporting Unit specialized behavior and typed results
Domain result, exception, event, provenance, custody and lifecycle semantics
prefectIntegrationResponsibilities: Bind Stage facade to native Stage Parent Workflow/Deployment invocation
Bind Step public callable to native nested Step Subworkflow
Bind executable SPUs and selected Supporting Unit functions to native executable elements
Map native execution context, parent/child correlation, operational identity and result retrieval without replacing domain identities
Translate Prefect operational state separately from GPWCF domain results
prefectNativeResponsibilities: Native Root/Stage/Step Flow execution and nesting
Scheduling, dispatch, worker assignment and native run/task records
Native evaluation/enactment of GPWCF-defined transition conditions within the declared integration boundary
consumerResponsibilities: Concrete Stage/Step/SPU and Supporting Unit specializations
Concrete Stage Flow Result contract and any required Step-specific result specializations
Concrete recovery, cancellation, retry and lifecycle policies not defined by reusable GPWCF contracts
evidenceLimits: PHASE-01 qualified native hierarchy and identity correlation using contract-shaped fixtures; it did not prove production GPWCF class binding.
PHASE-02 qualified a same-host two-Process-Worker deployment profile for sibling Stage overlap, parent linkage and Stage domain-result retrieval.
PHASE-02 does not qualify multi-host distribution/storage, more than two concurrent Stages, production GPWCF binding, supporting-unit binding, failure/recovery, or sibling Step concurrency.
Prefect operational State is execution evidence, not a replacement for SPUExecutionResult, StepExecutionResult or Stage Flow Result.
Prefect Flow Run, Task Run and Deployment identities remain distinct from GPWCF domain identities.
The 106-package Prefect environment snapshot is not a minimized GPWCF Prefect Integration dependency closure.

dependencyAndOwnershipConstraints: Python development/build/verification dependencies remain managed through the existing SMRB solution and .dependencies arrangement; this matrix does not create a parallel dependency directory.
GPWCF Core currently declares Python standard-library-only runtime dependencies; do not add Prefect to Core.
Prefect-specific third-party dependencies belong to the Prefect Integration package/extra and require a verified minimal dependency closure.
Generator-specific dependencies and runtime assets remain owned by PayloadDescriptionGenerator/SMRB and are not GPWCF package dependencies.
A file's current location under Architecture/Common does not establish generic ownership.
No dependency on Generator-private environment or assets is permitted from GPWCF Core or Prefect Integration.
openDesignQuestions: How will the generic Stage callable contract and Stage identity be made explicit without introducing a universal Pipeline Root abstraction?
How will Stage-specific Flow Result contracts be represented through the Core API without imposing a universal schema?

Which exact error-model clauses must be detached from Stage/SPU generic contracts, and whether a genuinely reusable error contract is needed, requires separate approval and is not decided by this matrix.
How will StepExecutionResult expose optional specialized result fields without making all optional supporting patterns mandatory imports or runtime dependencies?
